psychological_state.sentiment: focused and quietly urgent — the community distress is now close enough to feel personal, not just observed

chosen_actions.description: Make the first actual freelance outreach — not planning, not drafting, but a real ask. Contact Nicole at the healthcare network directly. Pitch a limited-scope project: a two-month social media audit and content calendar for their patient communications team. Frame it as a pilot engagement, low-risk for them, proof-of-concept for me. The freelance services menu I drafted at tick 5 gets used for the first time. I am pricing the engagement at $800 flat for the pilot — low enough that the answer is easy, high enough that it registers as professional. This is not about income right now. This is about having one client before I need one. Tamika Jefferson is pivoting into freelance marketing from the auto sector — she has hustle and she is motivated. The marketing freelance space in this community is about to get more crowded, not less. I move now.

Address the insurance gap directly. I have been carrying 'coverage: none' as a known vulnerability for multiple ticks and not acting on it. With employment rate at 73% and role security at 0.46, the scenario where I need individual coverage is no longer theoretical — it is a planning requirement. Spend two hours on the ACA marketplace and compare the two lowest-cost silver plans available in my zip code. Commit to enrolling this week. Budget $175/month as a line item. I have been running a $1,183 surplus — absorbing $175 for insurance still leaves me with a $1,008 monthly surplus and closes the one gap that would genuinely hurt me in a disruption. The status anxiety piece: I know there is something in my head that says 'people like me have employer coverage.' That story is how I kept ignoring this. I am letting it go.

internal_monologue: The spending index is at 42. Twenty-seven percent of people in this community are out of work. Patricia Hawkins is making the hard calls I watched her avoid for months. Tamika Jefferson — a salesperson at an auto dealership — is building a freelance marketing client list. I have been a marketing professional for nine years, I drafted my own services menu five ticks ago, and I have not sent a single real pitch. That is embarrassing in a way that cuts through the status anxiety. The freelance work is not a fallback anymore — it is a parallel track that I should have activated two ticks ago. And the insurance thing: I have known about this gap the whole time. I kept thinking of it as a future problem. The community around me is showing me what a future problem looks like when it arrives. I can afford $175 a month. I have been choosing not to spend it. That ends this tick. Two things, both executable today. Not planning. Doing.
